newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan boy killed by lion at "petting" zoo.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan boy killed by lion at "petting" zoo.

text.p: A Sri Lankan schoolboy was killed by a lion while posing for a picture with it at a popular "petting" zoo, police said on Friday.
Police in the tourist resort of Ahungalle, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo, said the 17-year-old boy died after he was mauled by the lion, the private zoo's star attraction.

"The boy had sat next to the lion to have his picture taken with the animal. The keeper had stepped aside so that he would not be in the picture. That is when it attacked," sub-inspector Saman Keerthi told Reuters.
Visitors to the zoo can enter the animals' cages and pet them. Leopards and a crocodile are also available for petting, police said.
Wildlife activists have previously criticised the zoo's owners for allegedly drugging the animals to allow petting.
The zoo's owners have denied the charge, saying the animals allowed be touched were tamed from years of contact with humans.
The owners, who closed the zoo on Friday as a mark of respect for the victim, were unavailable for comment.
